lines.t: The forest closes over the road like a hand. Pines the size of towers rise on either side, their needles silvered with frost, and every branch holds a little lantern of pale light.
Silverhush hangs among them, a town of curving white wood and glass, built along the boughs and around the trunks. Rope-bridges glitter with rime. Moon-pools lie in every clearing, as still as coins.
It is also silent. Not quiet. Silent. Elves cross the bridges with their mouths closed and their eyes down. A child opens her mouth to laugh, and her mother, gently, puts a finger across her lips.

The keep's high gallery is lined with banners of moon-silver, every one of them frozen stiff. At the far end stands an elf in white mail with a bow in one hand and a lantern in the other. The lantern burns pale, and nothing about its light is kind.
She speaks, and it is the first voice you have heard from an elf since the road. It is flat, as if read from a card.
The Hush is law. The Hush is peace. The Hush is mercy. You will be silent, or you will be silenced.
That lantern is not yours. Put it down.
The Hush is law. The Hush is peace.

The lantern slips from Aelith's hand and shatters. The pale light thins, and drifts away into the rafters like breath. For a long moment she stands swaying, and then she draws a ragged breath that sounds almost like a sob.
I heard myself. For three months I have heard myself say those words and I could not stop. A man in a pale coat gave me the lantern at the gate. He said it would keep the forest safe.

He went north to the frozen shrine at Rootmere, where the old treants keep the first root of the forest. He said he needed a place that remembered a sunrise. Go. Stop him. And tell Speaker Ilvaren that I am myself again.
The Chancellor. Always one step ahead, and always carrying a light that is not his.
